A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same G3Flow study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–B are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original robotic-manipulation simulation results, semantic-field comparisons, and measured field-generation speeds in Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds D3Fields (GenDP) comparison results and decision-frequency measurements in Tables 3–4.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same exploration, digital-twin generation, DINOv2/PCA features, pose tracking, and conditional diffusion policy. The additional asset-reuse explanation does not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same five RoboTwin tasks and seen/unseen object sets, documented in Figures 6–8 and Appendix A. The added comparisons reuse existing shoe tasks and occlusion scenarios.

E2.justification: v2 adds DP w/ D3Fields (GenDP) to the efficiency and two shoe-task comparisons in Tables 3–4. The scene-level comparator is retained, as are the DP, DP3, and DP3-with-color comparator sets in Tables 1–2.

E3.justification: v2 adds decision-making frequency to the existing field-generation speed evaluation. The RTX 4090 timing environment, main training budgets, demonstrations, test episodes, and object splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 expands the existing semantic-quality and efficiency analyses with D3Fields comparisons and decision-speed measurements. The revised feature visualization examines goal-image priors, gripper occlusion, and incomplete point clouds in greater detail.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three random seeds and report success-rate means and standard deviations. The added D3Fields results follow the existing reporting practice; no new repeated-run procedure, confidence interval, or significance test is introduced.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and existing ablation scores are unchanged. v2 adds D3Fields success rates of 73.7±2.5% and 20.3±6.8% for Shoe Place and Dual Shoes Place, plus an 8.14 Hz field-generation rate. New decision frequencies are 9.52 Hz for scene-level DINOv2, 6.89 Hz for D3Fields, and 34.04 Hz for G3Flow.

T1.justification: The pose transformation, denoising equation, training objective, and associated definitions in Equations 1–3 are mathematically unchanged. Neither version contains additional theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same semantic-flow contributions, occlusion-robustness claims, and headline success rates of 68.3% and 50.1%. The added analyses support the existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 newly explains D3Fields' advantage over raw scene-level features through goal-image priors, while identifying inaccurate semantics under gripper occlusion and incomplete single-view point clouds as remaining weaknesses. It also extends the real-time applicability discussion to decision-making speed.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly clarifies that digital assets are generated once per object and reused across multiple operations. Appendix B's implementation code, preprocessing, architecture, and hyperparameters remain unchanged, as does the project-access link.

R1.justification: v2 adds DexHandDiff to the diffusion-policy literature cited in Section 2.3 and expands discussion of the already-cited D3Fields/GenDP methods in Section 4.4. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 4.4 is locally rewritten and reordered to present efficiency before semantic quality. Section 4.5 gains a more specific heading, and an affiliation is abbreviated. Most other prose and the appendix structure are retained.

P2.justification: The two ablation tables are expanded and exchange numbering. v1 Figure 10 is replaced by v2 Figure 9's expanded feature comparison, while the five-task visualization becomes Figure 10. Figure 1 is restyled; its mismatch between task labels and plotted averages already exists in v1.

improvement.justification: Direct D3Fields/GenDP comparisons and decision-frequency measurements address a limited validation gap in v1, while the expanded visualization clarifies the occlusion argument. These gains modestly outweigh new reporting imprecision: the claimed 'nearly 6 times' decision-speed advantage is approximately 4.94 times according to Table 3.
